punchline: The plates matched. The appetite did not.
thirty_sec: In a 2019 NIH ward study led by Kevin Hall, 20 volunteers ate two weeks of ultra-processed food and two weeks of unprocessed food, with meals matched on nutrients. On the ultra-processed menu they ate about 508 more calories a day and gained 0.9 kg.
question: Which food last week looked harmless on its label but kept you eating more than you meant to?
